title: Grammar foundations
summary: Build complete thoughts with です and ます, then use particles to show what each noun is doing.
sourceFiles: 文法基礎　Basic grammar Noun・Adjectiveです　　Verbます  .pdf
takeaways: です sentences describe or identify.
ます sentences place an action in time.
Particles describe roles; they are not one-to-one English prepositions.

grammar.title: Identify with です
grammar.summary: Set a topic with は, then identify or describe it. Change です for negative or past time.
grammar.detail: です is polite and does not change for person. Japanese often omits a topic that is already obvious.

tokens.text: じゃありませんでした

grammar.caution: は is written ha but pronounced wa when it is the topic particle.

grammar.title: Place actions in time
grammar.summary: The ます family expresses polite non-past, negative, past, and past-negative actions.

examples.english: I wake up at eight every morning.

tokens.reading: はたらきませんでした

grammar.caution: Non-past ます covers both habits and future events. Time words provide the distinction.

grammar.title: Act on something
grammar.pattern: Place で Noun を Verb ます
grammar.summary: Use を for the thing directly affected and で for the place, tool, language, or means of the action.

examples.english: I write the paper in English.

recall.prompt: How do you make です past-negative?
recall.answer: じゃありませんでした
